This haiku is a masterpiece of the "light" style. There is no heavy philosophical burden or intense emotional outburst. This haiku captures the essence of *fūryū* (refined elegance). It celebrates the luxury of wasting time in the pursuit of beauty. The poet is so enchanted by the "far and near" of the blossoms that he loses track of time, his feet leading him back to the same paths day after day.
